### TAG-233: validate — entry invocation source shapes must match DUT source shapes

**Status:** ⬜ Not started

## Software Notes

An entry invocation supplies args to a definition. For the network wrapper to wire them together positionally, the *shapes* of the args must line up: flat place ↔ flat place, group ↔ group of the same kind (bundle, mutex, arbitration), same nesting depth. When they don't — e.g. `OR151($A $B)` against a DUT whose sources are `[{A0<> A1<>}] [{B0<> B1<>}]` — the wrapper generator can't reconstruct which flat value goes to which group member. It currently falls back to nulling the inputs, which produces a silently-broken wrapper.

The book's bundling convention (Fant §12.3.2) describes flat-to-group pairing as *intended* by the author, but the encoding — which flat value goes to which bundle member — isn't expressed in the syntax. The emitter can't decode it. The honest answer is to reject the mixed shape at validation time and require the author to spell both sides the same way.

This ticket adds that validation check.

## Background

[TAG-231](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-231/wrapper-generator-doesnt-handle-group-entry-args) made the wrapper generator expose named-place and group entry args as input ports when the shapes match (both flat, or both group of the same structure). Mixed-shape invocations fall back to the pre-TAG-231 behavior: no ports, all `arg_N` nulled. The fallback is defensive but silent — nothing tells the author their wrapper is dead.

Two specific cases in the current 32 examples:

`OR151` **— flat entry, grouped DUT.**

```
OR151($A $B)(Y< >)                                 ← flat entry, 2 args
OR151[({A0<> A1<>} {B0<> B1<>})({$0 $1})...]       ← grouped DUT, 2 group args
```

Top-level arg counts match (2 vs 2). Flattened counts don't (2 vs 4). The wrapper falls back to nulled `arg_N`; `or151_network` has no input ports; it's untestable.

`TAG-130`**'s** `FULLADD130(0 0 0)` **— numeric literals.**

Three `.place` args whose text is `0`/`0`/`0` (parsed as places because the parser reads bare digits as identifiers). These stay as `arg_N` + `data_value(0)` drives, which is correct (they're literal values, not ports). [TAG-231](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-231/wrapper-generator-doesnt-handle-group-entry-args) already handles this case correctly; the validation check shouldn't fire on it. It's mentioned here so the check's logic doesn't accidentally reject literals.

The check is specifically about *shape mismatch* between a flat place and a group, not about literal values.

## Goal

`validate.zig` gains a new check: for each top-level entry invocation, the source args' shapes must match the definition's source args' shapes. "Match" means:

* Same top-level `ArgKind` (`.place` ↔ `.place`, `.group` ↔ `.group`).
* For `.group` args, same `PlaceGroupKind` (`.bundle`, `.mutex`, `.arbitration`) and same `places.len`.
* Recursively, nested groups must match by the same rule.
* Literal-valued `.place` args (text parses as an integer) are exempt — they're not ports and have no DUT-side shape to match.

If any source arg's shape doesn't match the corresponding DUT source arg's shape, emit a clear error naming the entry, the position, both shapes, and a suggestion to flatten the invocation (or bundle the definition) so the shapes align.

## Proposed shape

New error variant:

```zig
pub const ValidationError = error{
    // ... existing variants ...
    /// An entry invocation's source arg has a different shape from the
    /// corresponding DUT source arg. See the book's bundling convention
    /// (Fant §12.3.2): flat and grouped shapes must correspond, or the
    /// wrapper generator cannot wire them positionally.
    EntrySourceShapeMismatch,
};
```

New check function, called from `checkNames` (or `checkInvocations`, wherever entry invocations are validated):

```zig
fn checkEntrySourceShapes(net: network.Network, diag: *Diagnostic) ValidationError!void {
    for (net.entries) |entry| {
        const matched = for (net.definitions) |d| {
            if (std.ascii.eqlIgnoreCase(d.name, entry.name)) break d;
        } else continue;  // UndefinedInvocation already caught this
        // Top-level arg count should already have been checked by the
        // wrapper generator; if they differ here, that's a separate
        // arity issue, not a shape issue. Skip.
        if (entry.sources.len != matched.sources.len) continue;
        for (entry.sources, matched.sources, 0..) |entry_arg, dut_arg, i| {
            try checkArgShapesMatch(entry_arg, dut_arg, entry.name, i, diag);
        }
    }
}
fn checkArgShapesMatch(
    entry_arg: network.Arg,
    dut_arg: network.Arg,
    entry_name: []const u8,
    index: usize,
    diag: *Diagnostic,
) ValidationError!void {
    // Literal entry arg: exempt from shape matching.
    if (entry_arg.kind == .place) {
        const text = std.mem.trim(u8, entry_arg.text, " \t\r\n");
        if (std.fmt.parseInt(u64, text, 10)) |_| return else |_| {}
    }
    if (entry_arg.kind != dut_arg.kind) {
        diag.* = .{ .name = entry_name, .in = "" };
        std.debug.print(
            "validation error: entry invocation '{s}' source arg {d} has kind '{s}', " ++
                "but the DUT's matching source arg has kind '{s}'. " ++
                "Flatten the entry arg to match (e.g. `$A0 $A1` instead of `$A`), " ++
                "or bundle the definition's sources to match the entry. " ++
                "Mixed flat/grouped shapes are not yet supported by the wrapper generator.\n",
            .{ entry_name, index, @tagName(entry_arg.kind), @tagName(dut_arg.kind) },
        );
        return error.EntrySourceShapeMismatch;
    }
    if (entry_arg.kind == .group) {
        const entry_grp = entry_arg.group orelse return;
        const dut_grp = dut_arg.group orelse return;
        if (entry_grp.kind != dut_grp.kind) {
            diag.* = .{ .name = entry_name, .in = "" };
            std.debug.print(
                "validation error: entry invocation '{s}' source arg {d} is a group of kind '{s}', " ++
                    "but the DUT's matching source arg is a group of kind '{s}'. " ++
                    "The group kinds must match.\n",
                .{ entry_name, index, @tagName(entry_grp.kind), @tagName(dut_grp.kind) },
            );
            return error.EntrySourceShapeMismatch;
        }
        if (entry_grp.places.len != dut_grp.places.len) {
            diag.* = .{ .name = entry_name, .in = "" };
            std.debug.print(
                "validation error: entry invocation '{s}' source arg {d} is a group with {d} member(s), " ++
                    "but the DUT's matching source arg has {d} member(s). " ++
                    "The member counts must match.\n",
                .{ entry_name, index, entry_grp.places.len, dut_grp.places.len },
            );
            return error.EntrySourceShapeMismatch;
        }
        for (entry_grp.places, dut_grp.places, 0..) |entry_member, dut_member, member_i| {
            try checkArgShapesMatch(entry_member, dut_member, entry_name, index, diag);
            _ = member_i;
        }
    }
}
```

Called from `checkNames`:

```zig
for (net.definitions) |def| {
    try checkNoNestedDefinitions(def, diag);
    try checkInvocations(net.definitions, def, diag);
}
try checkEntrySourceShapes(net, diag);  // NEW
```

And the `validate()` error-message switch gains a branch:

```zig
error.EntrySourceShapeMismatch => std.debug.print(
    "validation error: entry invocation shapes don't match the DUT (see above for details)\n",
    .{},
),
```

## What the error looks like for `OR151`

```
validation error: entry invocation 'OR151' source arg 0 has kind 'place',
but the DUT's matching source arg has kind 'group'.
Flatten the entry arg to match (e.g. `$A0 $A1` instead of `$A`),
or bundle the definition's sources to match the entry.
Mixed flat/grouped shapes are not yet supported by the wrapper generator.
```

The author's options:

1. Flatten the entry: `OR151($A0 $A1 $B0 $B1)(Y<>)` and correspondingly flatten the definition's sources to `(A0<> A1<> B0<> B1<>)`. That's the "spell both sides the same way" fix.
2. Or bundle both: `OR151({$A0 $A1} {$B0 $B1})(...)` with the DUT already having `[{A0<> A1<>}] [...]`. If bundling both sides matches shape-for-shape, it passes — but note that the DUT's `[{A0<> A1<>}]` has an outer bundle-of-mutex, so the entry would need `{[{$A0 $A1}]}`-style nesting to match. That's awkward; the flattening option is cleaner.

## Scope

* `validate.zig`**:** new error variant, new `checkEntrySourceShapes` function, new call in `checkNames`, new `validate()` error branch.
* `OR151`**'s example:** the current source is the shape-mismatched one. The validation error will fire until the source is fixed. **Two options:**
  * Fix `OR151`'s source to flatten both sides (recommended — the book's example text can be updated to show the flattened form alongside the bundled form, or the bundled form preserved if the wrapper-generator can be extended later).
  * Suppress the check for `OR151` temporarily with a comment, deferring the fix to a follow-up.

  I'd recommend fixing the source — a validation error that fires on a shipped example is noise until the example is fixed. Flattening `OR151`'s invocation and definition preserves the semantics, just without the sugar. The book text's example (shown above) can be updated to the flattened form, or kept as the "before" form the ticket's "why flatten" comment references.
* `TAG-130`**'s** `FULLADD130(0 0 0)`**:** the literal args are exempt via the `parseInt` check. No change needed.
* **Other examples:** `TAG-149`, `TAG-180`, `TAG-142`, `TAG-143`, `TAG-177` all have matching shapes (both flat, or both grouped). The check passes for them. `TAG-177`'s `FULLADD177(A B C)` — three flat `.place` args (non-numeric names `A`, `B`, `C`) against the DUT's three flat `.place` sources. Match. `TAG-177`'s check passes.
* **Tests:** add a unit test that constructs a `Network` with a mixed-shape entry invocation and asserts `validateWithDiagnostic` returns `EntrySourceShapeMismatch`. And a test that a matching-shape entry invocation passes. The existing `validate_test.zig` has the pattern for this.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `validate.zig` gains `EntrySourceShapeMismatch` and `checkEntrySourceShapes`.
2. `OR151`'s current source (or a copy thereof in a test fixture) produces a clear validation error naming the entry, the arg position, both kinds, and the suggested fix.
3. `OR151`'s shipped source is updated to flatten both sides (or the check is deferred with a TODO for that example). Flattening must preserve the DUT's semantics — the emitted VHDL's behavior for `OR151` should be unchanged after the source edit.
4. All other 31 examples still validate cleanly and remain green on GHDL syntax and simulation.
5. A unit test asserts the error fires for a mixed-shape fixture, and a matching-shape fixture passes.
6. `TAG-130`'s literal args (`0 0 0`) remain exempt — validation doesn't fire for them.

## Non-goals

* **Wrapper-generator support for mixed shapes.** This ticket rejects mixed shapes; it doesn't make the wrapper handle them. A future ticket could, if a viable encoding convention emerges (the emitter doesn't have one without author-supplied information).
* **Detecting numeric literal entry args as a validation error.** TAG-130's `0 0 0` is a correct usage (three constant inputs), and the wrapper handles it as `arg_N + data_value(0)`. Don't flag it.
* **Validating destination shapes.** The destination side already flattens correctly in the wrapper generator (via `collectBoundaryPortNamesInto`), and `OR151`'s destination `Y<>` against the DUT's `[{$0 $1}]` happens to work because the destination-side flattening pairs by boundary position. A destination-side shape check might be worth doing later, but it's not blocking anything today.

## Notes for the implementer

* **The** `parseInt` **exemption must match the wrapper generator's logic.** TAG-231's `writeOneNetworkEntity` uses `std.fmt.parseInt(u64, trimmed, 10)` to distinguish numeric literals (stay `arg_N`) from named places (become ports). The validation check must use the same predicate, or it will flag a case the wrapper handles correctly.
* **Recursive checks are cheap.** `checkArgShapesMatch` recurses into nested groups. `[{A0 A1}]` (bundle of mutex) vs `{$A0 $A1}` (mutex) differ at the top level (bundle vs mutex), so the check fires before recursing. Two matching structures (`[{A0 A1}]` on both sides) recurse to verify the inner mutex members match. For the examples in the corpus, nesting is at most two deep.
* **Error message quality matters here.** The whole point of this ticket is to catch a mistake the author made and tell them how to fix it. The message should name the entry, the arg position, both kinds, and give a concrete example of the flattened form. The `OR151` case: "source arg 0 has kind 'place', but the DUT's matching source arg has kind 'group'. Flatten the entry arg to match (e.g. `$A0 $A1` instead of `$A`)..." That's actionable.
* `OR151`**'s source fix is part of the ticket.** Without it, the ticket ships a validation error that immediately fires on a shipped example. Either flatten the source as part of the same commit, or add a temporary `@validate-off` marker (if the validate module has such a mechanism) with a TODO. Flattening the source is cleaner and preserves the check's value — the author learns the pattern by seeing it in the shipped example.

## Related

* [TAG-231](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-231/wrapper-generator-doesnt-handle-group-entry-args) — the wrapper-generator fix that added ports for matching shapes and falls back to null for mixed shapes. This ticket moves the mixed-shape case from "silently broken" to "explicitly rejected."
* **Fant §12.3.2** (the book text on bundling/unbundling) — the convention this ticket enforces shape-wise. The convention itself remains supported for matching shapes; only mixed shapes are rejected.
* [TAG-149](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-149/example-129-mutually-exclusive-completeness) — a matching-shape example that works end-to-end.
* [TAG-151](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-151/example-1217-bundling-mutually-exclusive-path-into-a-single-path) — the mixed-shape example this ticket's error will fire on.
